privacyPage.seoDescription: How FitFusion handles your data: what we collect, how we use it, and your rights. We keep data collection to a minimum.
privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.intro: Your privacy matters to us. This policy explains what information FitFusion collects, how we use it, and the choices you have. In short: we collect as little as possible.
privacyPage.dataText: Calculator inputs (such as height, weight, and age) are processed entirely in your browser and are never sent to or stored on our servers. The only personal information we store is your email address, and only if you voluntarily subscribe to our newsletter.
privacyPage.useText: If you subscribe to our newsletter, we use your email address solely to send you our newsletter with nutrition science, training tips, and product updates. We never sell, rent, or share your email address with third parties for marketing purposes.
privacyPage.newsletterText: You can unsubscribe from our newsletter at any time. Once you unsubscribe, we stop sending you emails.
privacyPage.cookiesText: We use your browser's local storage to remember your preferences, such as your language and light/dark theme choice. This data stays on your device. We do not use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.
privacyPage.thirdPartyText: Our website is hosted on cloud infrastructure that may log basic technical data (such as IP addresses) for security and reliability purposes. Social sharing buttons only contact the respective platform when you actively click them.
privacyPage.rightsText: You have the right to access, correct, or delete the personal data we hold about you (your newsletter email address). To exercise these rights, contact us through the channels listed on our Contact page and we will respond promptly.
privacyPage.changesText: We may update this policy from time to time. Any changes will be posted on this page with an updated revision date.

bmiCalculator.title: BMI Calculator
bmiCalculator.description: Calculate your Body Mass Index (BMI) to understand your weight category and health status
bmiCalculator.enterInfo: Enter your information and click Calculate
bmiCalculator.underweightDescription: You are underweight. Consider consulting a healthcare provider about healthy weight gain strategies.
bmiCalculator.normalWeightDescription: You are at a healthy weight. Maintain your current lifestyle with balanced nutrition and regular exercise.
bmiCalculator.overweightDescription: You are overweight. Consider a balanced diet and increased physical activity to reach a healthier weight.
bmiCalculator.obeseDescription: You are in the obese category. Consult a healthcare provider for a personalized weight management plan.
bmiCalculator.aboutDescription: Body Mass Index (BMI) is a measure of body fat based on height and weight. It's used as a screening tool to identify possible weight problems. However, BMI is not diagnostic and should be used alongside other health assessments.
bmiCalculator.limitationsDescription: BMI doesn't account for muscle mass, bone density, overall body composition, and racial and sex differences. Athletes or very muscular individuals may have high BMI without excess body fat.

bmrCalculator.title: BMR Calculator
bmrCalculator.description: Calculate your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) - the calories your body burns at rest
bmrCalculator.aboutDescription: Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) is the number of calories your body needs to accomplish its most basic (basal) life-sustaining functions. This calculation uses the Mifflin-St Jeor Equation, which is considered the most accurate formula for most people.
bmrCalculator.formulaMale: Men: BMR = (10 × weight in kg) + (6.25 × height in cm) - (5 × age in years) + 5
bmrCalculator.formulaFemale: Women: BMR = (10 × weight in kg) + (6.25 × height in cm) - (5 × age in years) - 161
bmrCalculator.whatItMeansDescription: Your body burns approximately {bmr} calories per day at complete rest. This is the energy needed for basic life-sustaining functions like breathing, circulation, and cell production.
bmrCalculator.additionalInfo: Your BMR accounts for about 60-75% of your total daily energy expenditure. Factors like muscle mass, genetics, and hormones can affect your actual BMR. For total daily calorie needs, you must multiply your BMR by your activity level factor.

calorieCalculator.title: Daily Calorie Calculator
calorieCalculator.description: Calculate your daily calorie needs based on your activity level and goals
calorieCalculator.extraActive: Extra active (very hard exercise & physical job)
calorieCalculator.resultDescription: Based on your activity level, you need approximately {calories} calories per day to maintain your current weight.
calorieCalculator.aboutDescription: Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) is the total number of calories you burn each day, including your basal metabolic rate and physical activity. It's calculated by multiplying your BMR by an activity factor.
calorieCalculator.safeWeightLossDescription: To lose weight, create a calorie deficit by eating fewer calories than your TDEE. For weight gain, eat more. A deficit of 500 calories per day typically results in about 1 pound of weight loss per week. Always consult healthcare professionals before making significant dietary changes.

macroCalculator.title: Macronutrient Calculator
macroCalculator.description: Calculate your optimal protein, carbs, and fat intake for your fitness goals
macroCalculator.useCalculator: Use the Daily Calorie Calculator to find your target
macroCalculator.resultDescription: These macronutrient targets are optimized for your {goal} goal. Track your daily intake to ensure you're meeting these targets for best results.
macroCalculator.aboutDescription: Macronutrients (macros) are the nutrients your body needs in large amounts: protein, carbohydrates, and fats. Each provides energy (calories) and plays unique roles in your health and fitness.
macroCalculator.proteinRole: Protein (4 calories per gram): Essential for muscle repair and growth. Higher protein intake helps preserve muscle during weight loss and supports muscle building.
macroCalculator.carbsRole: Carbohydrates (4 calories per gram): Your body's primary energy source. Important for workout performance and recovery. Lower carbs may help with fat loss.
macroCalculator.fatRole: Fats (9 calories per gram): Crucial for hormone production and nutrient absorption. Don't go too low as fats are essential for health.
macroCalculator.choosingSplitDescription: These are general recommendations. Individual needs vary based on factors like training intensity, metabolism, and personal preferences. Adjust as needed based on your progress.

tips.title: Fitness Tips for Beginners & Returning Athletes

whyExercise.title: Why Regular Exercise Matters
whyExercise.intro: Regular physical activity is one of the most important things you can do for your health. No matter your age or fitness level, the benefits of exercise are truly transformative.

cardiovascular.title: Heart Health
cardiovascular.description: Strengthens your heart, improves circulation, and reduces risk of cardiovascular disease

mental.title: Mental Well-being
mental.description: Reduces stress, anxiety, and depression while boosting mood and self-confidence

strength.title: Physical Strength
strength.description: Builds muscle, increases bone density, and improves overall physical capability

flexibility.title: Flexibility & Balance
flexibility.description: Enhances mobility, prevents falls, and maintains independence as you age

beginnerTips.title: Essential Tips for Beginners
beginnerTips.intro: Starting your fitness journey can feel overwhelming, but these simple tips will help you build a strong foundation:
beginnerTips.tip1: Start where you are - Don't compare yourself to others. Every expert was once a beginner. Your journey is unique to you.
beginnerTips.tip2: Consistency beats intensity - It's better to do a moderate workout regularly than an intense workout once in a while. Aim for sustainable progress.
beginnerTips.tip3: Listen to your body - Some muscle soreness is normal, but sharp pain is a warning sign. Rest when needed and don't push through pain.
beginnerTips.tip4: Celebrate small wins - Did you work out today? That's a victory! Progress isn't always visible on the scale or in the mirror.
beginnerTips.tip5: Make it enjoyable - Choose activities you actually like. Exercise shouldn't feel like punishment. Dance, swim, hike, or play sports you enjoy.

buildingRoutine.title: Building Your Fitness Routine
buildingRoutine.intro: Creating a sustainable fitness routine is key to long-term success. Here's how to build one that works for you:

step1.title: Start Slowly and Progress Gradually
step1.description: Begin with 2-3 short sessions per week (even 10-15 minutes counts!). Gradually increase duration and intensity over weeks and months. This prevents burnout and injury.

step2.title: Set Realistic, Specific Goals
step2.description: Instead of 'get fit,' try 'walk 20 minutes three times a week' or 'do 10 push-ups.' Specific goals give you clear targets to work toward and celebrate.

step3.title: Schedule Your Workouts
step3.description: Treat exercise like an important appointment. Put it in your calendar and protect that time. Morning workouts can be great for consistency.

step4.title: Mix Different Types of Exercise
step4.description: Include cardio (walking, running, cycling), strength training (bodyweight or weights), and flexibility work (stretching, yoga) for balanced fitness.

step5.title: Track Your Progress
step5.description: Keep a simple log of your workouts. Seeing your consistency and improvements over time is incredibly motivating and helps you stay accountable.

injury.title: Injury Prevention & Proper Form
injury.intro: Staying injury-free is crucial for maintaining your fitness journey. Follow these guidelines to exercise safely:
injury.injury1: Always warm up for 5-10 minutes with light cardio and dynamic stretching before your workout to prepare your muscles.
injury.injury2: Focus on proper form over heavy weights or high intensity. If you're unsure, watch instructional videos or consider working with a trainer initially.
injury.injury3: Cool down after exercise with gentle stretching. This helps reduce muscle soreness and improves flexibility over time.
injury.injury4: Progress gradually - increase workout intensity or duration by no more than 10% per week to give your body time to adapt.

recovery.title: Rest, Recovery & Nutrition
recovery.intro: Recovery is just as important as exercise itself. Your body gets stronger during rest, not during the workout:
recovery.recovery1: Get 7-9 hours of quality sleep each night. This is when your body repairs and builds muscle. Poor sleep undermines your fitness efforts.
recovery.recovery2: Take at least 1-2 rest days per week. Rest days don't mean being completely sedentary - light walking or gentle yoga is great.
recovery.recovery3: Fuel your body with balanced nutrition. Include plenty of protein for muscle repair, complex carbs for energy, and healthy fats for overall health.
recovery.recovery4: Stay hydrated throughout the day, not just during exercise. Water is essential for every bodily function and optimal performance.

motivation.title: You've Got This!
motivation.message: Remember, starting is the hardest part. Every workout is an investment in your future self. Be patient with yourself, stay consistent, and celebrate every step forward. You're capable of more than you think!
motivation.quote: The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step. Take that step today.

safety.title: Supplement Safety Guidelines
safety.intro: Follow these essential safety tips to supplement responsibly:
safety.tip1: Read labels carefully - Check for third-party certification (USP, NSF, Informed-Sport) to ensure quality and purity. Avoid proprietary blends that don't disclose exact amounts.
safety.tip2: Start with one supplement at a time - This helps you identify any adverse reactions and understand what works for your body.
safety.tip3: Respect recommended dosages - More is not better. Excessive intake can cause side effects and waste money. Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) can build up to toxic levels.
safety.tip4: Consider timing and interactions - Some supplements interact with medications or other supplements. Take calcium and iron separately, as they compete for absorption.
safety.tip5: Store properly and check expiration dates - Keep supplements in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Discard expired products as potency decreases over time.

avoid.title: Supplements to Avoid or Use with Extreme Caution
avoid.intro: These supplements are often unnecessary, potentially harmful, or lack scientific evidence:
avoid.avoid1: Weight loss pills and 'fat burners' - Often contain stimulants that can be dangerous, unproven ingredients, or are simply ineffective. Focus on diet and exercise instead.
avoid.avoid2: Anabolic steroids and prohormones - Illegal without prescription, serious health risks including liver damage, heart problems, and hormonal imbalances.
avoid.avoid3: Mega-dose vitamins - Taking vitamins far above the recommended daily intake can be toxic (especially vitamins A, D, E, K) and may increase health risks.
avoid.avoid4: Unregulated supplements from unknown sources - Products bought from unreliable websites or containing exotic ingredients may be contaminated, mislabeled, or contain banned substances.

finalNote.title: Remember: Food First, Supplements Second
finalNote.message: The best nutrition comes from a varied, balanced diet rich in whole foods. Supplements are meant to fill specific gaps, not replace healthy eating. Prioritize quality sleep, regular exercise, stress management, and whole foods before turning to supplements.
